name: Liu Ming Chung
forbes_bio: Liu Ming Chung leads Nine Dragons Paper, one of Asia's largest paper producers.
Hong Kong-listed Nine Dragons started out as a supplier of packaging for exporters in China, and now also benefits from consumer demand inside China.
Liu is CEO and deputy chairman of Nine Dragons, while his wife Cheung Yan, also a billionaire, is the chairlady. They are both cofounders of the company, which was established in 1995.
Liu was born in Taiwan and grew up in Brazil. He holds a bachelor's degree in dental surgery from the University of Santo Amaro, in Brazil.
His son Ken Liu joined Nine Dragons' board of directors in 2018, after graduating from Harvard University and working as a consultant for PwC.
forbes_facts: His wife Cheung has been dubbed by Chinese media as the country's "wastepaper queen." Liu and Cheung met in Hong Kong and married in the US.

name: Murli Dhar
forbes_bio: Low profile brothers Murli Dhar and Bimal Gyanchandani control family's Kanpur-headquartered consumer goods firm RSPL Group.
RSPL is best known for its low-cost Ghari detergent, which is popular in north India.
Murli Dhar's two sons work in the group, along with Bimal's son Rohit, after whom the flagship Rohit Surfactants is named.
The brothers' other interests include real estate and footwear under the Red Chief brand.
forbes_facts: The siblings have set up a charitable hospital in Kanpur named after their parents.

name: Caryn Seidman-Becker
forbes_bio: Caryn Seidman-Becker is cofounder and CEO of Clear Secure, which uses identification technology for security checkpoints at airports and stadiums.
A former hedge fund manager, she and a colleague bought Clear's predecessor out of bankruptcy in 2010.
In 2023 she expanded the company's identity-confirming services into digital healthcare records. This plus strong travel demand helped revenue grow to $900 million in 2025.
After raising capital from investors including airlines Delta and United, she took the company public in June 2021 at a $4 billion valuation.
She joined Home Depot's board of directors in 2022 and, previously, sat on the board of fintech Lemonade.

name: Kerr Neilson
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2008-2022); Hurun Global (2014-2022); Wikidata (2016)
forbes_bio: Kerr Neilson owns more than 40% of international equities fund manager Platinum Asset Management together with his ex-wife Judith.
They had partially cashed out in a well-timed 2007 IPO.
Known for his value-based contrarian stock picks that have earned him comparisons with Warren Buffett, Neilson bought his first stock at age 13.
A Johannesburg native, he cofounded Platinum in 1994, after moving to Sydney from South Africa a decade earlier to work for Bankers Trust Australia.
In 2020 he retired from Platinum Asset and remains a non-executive director; he supervises the assets of the Neilson Foundation and his own portfolio.

name: Steven Roth
sec_insider_companies: VORNADO REALTY TRUST (VNO) - CHAIRMAN AND CEO
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2020); Forbes annual (2006-2019); Hurun Global (2020); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Steven Roth is chairman and CEO of real estate investment trust Vornado Realty Trust.
Vornado owns more than 20 million square feet of Manhattan office and retail space, plus properties in San Francisco and Chicago.
Vornado owns two buildings alongside Donald Trump: 1290 Avenue of the Americas in New York City and 555 California Street in San Francisco.
Roth served as an economic advisor to Trump's 2016 campaign, and was tapped for a spot on the president's short-lived infrastructure council.
His wife, Daryl, is a Broadway and off-Broadway producer.
forbes_facts: Roth purchased Bernie Madoff's Hamptons estate in October 2009 for $9.4 million.
Roth once served on the boards of J.C. Penney and Toys 'R' Us.

name: Aldo Bensadoun
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2021); Forbes annual (2015-2020); Hurun Global (2015-2026)
forbes_bio: Aldo Bensadoun is the founder of Canadian retailer ALDO, best known for its footwear and accessories.
The son of a shoe merchant and grandson of a cobbler, Bensadoun was born in Morocco and spent most of his childhood in France.
Upon moving to Montreal for college, he opened ALDO as a concession within a chain of popular fashion boutiques in 1972.
His son, David, who is now the CEO, joined the company in 1996 and became the fourth generation of his family to work in the shoe business.
ALDO pulled in an estimated $1.5 billion in sales in 2019 and has more than 3,000 stores across the world.

name: Shunji Sugaya
forbes_bio: Shunji Sugaya founded Optim, the cloud and remote working service provider, in 2000.
Optim listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange's Mothers section for startups in 2014 and moved to the First Section the next year.
The company posted over $63 million in revenue in the fiscal year ended in March 2020 and about $1 million in net profit.
Working from home during the coronavirus pandemic spurred demand for Optim's remote working tools, boosting its stock price.
forbes_facts: A self-taught programmer, Sugaya began coding software to create games, which he sold to his friends while still in high school.
In 2000, Japanese billionaire Masayoshi Son offered to buy out his startup idea, but Sugaya turned him down because he wanted to set up his own business.

name: Lisheng Yao
forbes_bio: Yao is a director of Maxscend Microelectronics, a supplier of smartphone radio frequency switches.
Maxscend Microelectronics was founded in 2012 by a group of Silicon Valley alums.
Yao holds a master's degree from the Chinese Academy of Sciences.
